paragraphs: On Saturday morning, Lily and Leo went to Mia's house for a science test. Mia's dad opened the garage, where he fixes bikes. There was an old refrigerator in the corner, and two balls were on the table. The three children stood in a line with a pencil and a paper. "Today you test one question," he said. "Does a cold ball bounce lower than a warm ball?" "I will say the steps. You must follow them in order."

"Step one, put one ball in the refrigerator for one hour." "The other ball stays on the table, so it stays warm." "Step two, make ten marks on the wall with a pencil." "Write the numbers from one to ten next to the marks. Start at the floor." Mia's dad looked at the digital camera on the table. "The battery is low," he said, and he plugged it in. "It needs a little electricity before we start."

"Step three, take the cold ball out of the refrigerator after one hour." "Hold it at mark ten and drop it on the flat floor." "Lily, you watch the wall. Say the mark where the ball goes up." "Mia, you film each drop with the digital camera." "Leo, you write each number in the table." "For example, if the ball goes up to mark seven, you write seven."

"Step four, drop each ball three times. Write all three numbers." "Why three times?" asked Leo. "One drop may be a mistake," said Mia's dad, "but three drops give a better answer." "Every drop must start at mark ten." "Step five, put the old carpet on the floor and do the same test again." "What if the ball hits the wall?" asked Lily. "Then drop it again," he said. "That drop is not good. We want good numbers."

After one hour, Mia took the cold ball out of the refrigerator. Lily watched the wall. Leo wrote the numbers in the table. On the flat floor, the cold ball went up to mark five. The warm ball went up to mark seven. On the carpet, both balls went up much less. The carpet was soft, and the balls stopped fast. Leo laughed because he saw the ball stop on the carpet. "So we have an answer," said Mia. "A cold ball bounces lower, and a carpet makes every ball bounce lower." Mia's dad smiled, because the three children followed every step.
